label: Portal-seeded volume-filling CCO tree with anisotropic surface-terminal refinement

assumptions.method: single-tree CCO-inspired growth from the observed portal root, using volume-optimized jittered bifurcations and one global candidate-edge search, extended by coverage-driven adaptive growth (targets the worst-covered tissue directly rather than a fixed terminal count or reactive edge-length patching), followed by long-tail densification (any unbranched leaf reach over the short-reach length cap is recursively bisected with a real side-branch child at each split, so long bare reaches resolve into multiple generations of bifurcation rather than staying as a single long unbranched segment)
assumptions.centrelineMethod: cubic Hermite per element (blend=0.4, 8 render/quadrature samples); root derivative seeded from the observed truncated tree measured tangent
assumptions.coverageMethod: Monte Carlo tissue sampling (3000 pts/iteration); target 92% of tissue within 7.0mm of a vessel; worst-covered points (min separation 2.5mm) added in batches of up to 25 per iteration
assumptions.boundaryTargetMethod: No forced surface shell; terminal contact with the liver boundary emerges from uniform interior perfusion targets and containment/length constraints
assumptions.geometricConstraints: length>2x radius (all 3 segments), new-segment length<50x its radius, weak orientation sign checks, daughter radius ratio r_new/r_continuation>=0.3, radius-proportional clearance (>5x radius), distance-to-organ-skin length cap, perpendicular bifurcation jitter (non-collinear splits)
assumptions.surfaceTerminalRefinement: 114 leaves within 5.0 mm of the liver surface were converted into short inward/tangential daughter bifurcations. New segments were retained only when sampled inside the liver.
